intended_object: Given an ordered partition c of {0,…,n-1} into blocks, this is the composition map (f, (p_i)) ↦ (v ↦ f(p_1(v restricted to block 1), …, p_k(v restricted to block k))). It is packaged as a continuous linear map in f whose values are continuous multilinear maps in the family (p_i). The docstring and the Faà di Bruno module say so. It is the operator behind the terms of the Faà di Bruno formula.
explanation: The body applies `MultilinearMap.mkContinuousLinear` to the linear/multilinear version `compAlongOrderedFinpartitionₗ` with bound constant 1. That version is built from `compAlongOrderedFinpartition f p = f ∘ applyOrderedFinpartition p`, the composition along the partition blocks. The bound is justified by the estimate ‖c.compAlongOrderedFinpartition f p‖ ≤ ‖f‖ * ∏ ‖p i‖. So the result is exactly the continuous bilinear/multilinear composition operator described in the docstring. The setting is a nontrivially normed field with normed spaces E, F, G. That is the standard setting for continuous multilinear maps in Mathlib, so the definition is not too narrow. I found no other declaration of this operator in Mathlib. It serves as a building block for the Faà di Bruno formula, but it is a well-defined mathematical operator, and the definition matches it.
